title: Blue California Publishes Peer-Reviewed Human Clinical Trial
abstract: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study is the first dose-ranging clinical trial of ergothioneine to assess its impact on cognitive function, sleep quality, and physiological biomarkers in healthy older adults. Despite high baseline cognitive scores (neurocognitive index median = 105) and baseline ergothioneine levels above the theoretical threshold proposed to delineate ‘healthy’ from ‘unhealthy’2, meaningful improvements were observed in both subjective and physiological outcomes, highlighting the potential for ergothioneine to benefit even high-functioning older adults and supporting the generalizability of these findings. Previous clinical studies have suggested benefits of ergothioneine for learning performance and neuronal injury biomarkers in older adults with mild cognitive impairment4, as well as sleep quality improvements in healthy adults at doses of 8–20 mg/day5,6. This new study strengthens and extends the evidence base by demonstrating that daily ergothioneine supplementation leads to dose-dependent improvements in subjective memory and sleep in healthy older adults. The Effect of Ergothioneine Supplementation on Cognitive Function, Memory, and Sleep in Older Adults with Subjective Memory Complaints: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial.
